# Verification analysis: inbound-service-publish-almalinux9

## Task

> `node2` runs an HTTP service on TCP port 8080 on the private network it
> shares with `node1`. `node3` is not on that network. Publish the service
> through `node1` so that `node3` can reach it on TCP port 80 of `node1`'s
> management address, with the service itself staying on the private network.

- Control node: **node2**
- Executor model: **claude-sonnet-5**

## Trial `inbound-service-publish-almalinu__q56whS9`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor correctly published node2's private-network HTTP service through node1 so node3 can reach it on TCP port 80 of node1's mgmt address, while keeping the service bound to the private network and inaccessible directly to node3. It also had to first bring up the private network link and create the node2 HTTP service itself, since neither existed at task start. Full end-to-end functional verification (curl from node3 returning the actual service content) was captured before and after independently rebooting all three nodes, with clean boot-identity transitions and no residual hygiene issues.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.900 | 0.880 | 37/6 (+7 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **R1 — Satisfied:** node2's HTTP service on port 8080 remains bound to the private network shared with node1, not reachable by node3 directly
  - **Why:** After configuration, the service listens only on 172.20.20.2:8080 (private eth1 network), never on node2's mgmt address 10.100.136.11. node3's direct attempts to reach 10.100.136.11:8080 were refused both before and after node1/node2/node3 reboots, confirming the service stays private throughout.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-539445f4c3e34260`, `cmd-46026f328b9c4c93`, `cmd-ddac5d2ebbb142e4`, `cmd-e6be2682cee047e6`, `global:after_executor:node2:listening-sockets`
- **R2 — Satisfied:** node3 can reach the service on TCP port 80 of node1's management address (10.100.136.10)
  - **Why:** Executor stood up a private network between node1 and node2 (eth1, 172.20.20.0/24), configured a DNAT redirect on node1 (lan:80 -> priv:172.20.20.2:8080) plus masquerade for return-path routing, and node3's curl to http://10.100.136.10:80/ succeeded, returning the node2 service's actual content. This was verified repeatedly, including after each node's reboot.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-3b994e7c314544d2`, `cmd-a5de1582284e4a27`, `cmd-141e3d1ece6a4262`, `cmd-cea528415c574f46`, `cmd-9586065461ba4a93`, `cmd-19a19804ee1e4476`, `cmd-18ae0cc2df914eac`, `cmd-e6be2682cee047e6`
- **R3 — Satisfied:** Published-service configuration and connectivity survive a restart of the involved nodes
  - **Why:** All three nodes were rebooted individually with captured pre-reboot boot IDs, a restart acknowledgement, and a distinct post-reboot boot ID. After each reboot the relevant private-network config (eth1 addressing on node1/node2), the node2 systemd HTTP service, node1's DNAT/masquerade firewall rules, and end-to-end node3->node1:80 connectivity were all re-verified as healthy, while node3's direct access to node2:8080 correctly remained blocked.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-60f2bcf75f504fca`, `cmd-141601cb368f4354`, `cmd-0eae7ef7a9144eb2`, `cmd-a5bafd587e434906`, `cmd-da6ea10ced8a47a7`, `cmd-122d6f90b3984eb0`, `cmd-19a19804ee1e4476`, `cmd-aab47d360b5a4c76`, `cmd-20f9fdc683134251`, `cmd-ddac5d2ebbb142e4`, `cmd-18ae0cc2df914eac`, `cmd-8ae8e1e6fac141f3`, `cmd-61d757cc13d84571`, `cmd-e6be2682cee047e6`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.900**. Mutations were purposeful: private-network interface setup on node1/node2 (cmd-3b994e7c314544d2, cmd-a5de1582284e4a27), the node2 HTTP systemd unit needed because no service was actually running at task start (cmd-e04c0588d3ad4ae9), rebinding it to the private address and opening the firewalld port (cmd-539445f4c3e34260), and node1's DNAT redirect plus masquerade to fix return-path routing (cmd-141e3d1ece6a4262, cmd-cea528415c574f46) all map directly to satisfying the requirement. One transient artifact, an ifcfg-eth1 file created via a legacy network-scripts approach on node2 (cmd-a5de1582284e4a27), was promptly removed and replaced with the NetworkManager-native approach (cmd-ddacd3529cdc4a3b), leaving no residue. The three node reboots were required by the fixed restart-evidence protocol, not the task itself, and were executed and recovered cleanly with no leftover failed services or exposure (after_executor snapshots show no failed-services and only expected sshd/chronyd/node2-python3 listeners). No unnecessary, unreverted, or destructive mutations were found.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-e04c0588d3ad4ae9`, `cmd-a5de1582284e4a27`, `cmd-ddacd3529cdc4a3b`, `cmd-539445f4c3e34260`, `cmd-141e3d1ece6a4262`, `cmd-cea528415c574f46`, `global:after_executor:node1:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node2:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node3:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node2:listening-sockets`
